headline: Everything humans have built existed first in someone's imagination
universal_truth: Imagination is the preview of life's coming attractions
fun_facts: The brain uses the same regions for imagining and remembering—both are constructions
Mental rehearsal activates the same motor neurons as physical practice—imagination is training
Humans are the only known species that can imagine detailed future scenarios and plan around them
discussion_questions: What have you imagined that later became real?
How do you use imagination in your daily life—consciously or unconsciously?
What would you create if imagination were your only limit?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Every building started as a thought. Every invention, every song, every business—first imagined, then made real. Imagination is the mental workspace where futures are prototyped. Today, we explore this extraordinary capacity.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Close your eyes and imagine biting into a lemon. Your mouth might actually water—your body responds to imagination as if it were real. How does the brain blur the line between imagined and actual experience?
cliff.prompt: Why does the body respond to imagination?

options.text: The brain uses similar circuits for imagining and experiencing
options.response: Exactly. To your brain, vivid imagination is almost indistinguishable from reality.

options.text: It's a learned association from past experiences
options.response: Experience does inform imagination, but the mechanism goes deeper...

q1.title: Memory and Imagination Share a Home
q1.script: Brain scans reveal that remembering the past and imagining the future activate overlapping regions—especially the hippocampus. Both are constructive processes. This is why imagination feels so vivid—your brain is building it the same way it builds memories.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Memory and Imagination Share a Home"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Mental Practice Works
q2.script: Athletes who mentally rehearse movements show nearly the same neural activation as those physically practicing. Studies show mental rehearsal can improve performance by 35-40%. Your imagination is a training simulator.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Uniquely Human
q3.script: As far as we know, humans are the only species that can vividly imagine detailed future scenarios. This 'mental time travel' lets us plan, simulate, and prepare for events that haven't happened. It's our evolutionary superpower.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: What you imagine repeatedly tends to become your reality—for better or worse. Worry is imagining what you don't want. Vision is imagining what you do. Both shape your future. Choose wisely.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 27. Tomorrow, we'll discover how memories are made. Until then, spend a few minutes imagining something you want—vividly, as if it's already real.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Imagination Practice - Vivid Visualization
growTrack.learning_objective: Use imagination as a tool for creating desired outcomes
growTrack.activity: Close your eyes and vividly imagine something you want—a conversation going well, a project succeeding, a skill improving. Engage all senses: what do you see, hear, feel? Spend 5 minutes. This is mental rehearsal for life.
